name: Coach Bob!
tagline: An AR warm-up game on a punching dummy: glasses show where to strike, a voice coach heckles you, and a motion sensor scores each hit.
problem: Athletes skip or rush warm-ups because they are boring, and that leads to strains and lost training time.
solution: AR glasses project coloured targets onto a freestanding punching dummy to call kicks, knees and punches; a voice coach built on an LLM and a speech service eggs the athlete on; a motion sensor reads the dummy's wobble after impact to register hits and estimate force, and a dashboard shows speed, force and time after the session.
demo_moment: Team-described: put on the glasses, the dummy lights up with the next strike, the coach shouts, and every hit shows up on the dashboard.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Selected by the organizer as one of 12 finalists among 261 submissions.
Grew from a teammate missing a national Taekwondo competition after a strain blamed on a rushed warm-up.
Without a force sensor, the team measured hits from the dummy's wobble with a cheap motion sensor.
A physical dummy that people can hit puts the judges inside the demo rather than in front of a screen.

lessons: When a sensor is missing, measure the effect it would detect (here, the wobble) with what you have.
